items.title: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities
items.summary: N-able released hotfixes to address zero-day bugs affecting its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, which were publicly disclosed over the weekend and forced it to take vulnerable hosted environments offline.
instructions: In a Tuesday update , N-able said that all hosted N-central servers (NCODs) across all regions have now been successfully upgraded and advised and "strongly" recommended that all N-central On-Premises customers upgrade their installations to the newly released version "as soon as possible."
"Customers should follow the published upgrade guidance carefully before restoring normal access to their N-central environment.
Earlier incident guidance advised On-Premises customers to keep their N-central servers offline while remediation was being developed," it said.

This follows N-able's decision to take all hosted N-central environments offline across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific regions until it could patch them against potential attacks targeting the zero-day flaws in the wild.

items.title: New N-able "4EverAble2Shell" zero-day exploited hours after PoC released
items.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a newly disclosed N-able N-central zero-day vulnerability dubbed "4EverAble2Shell" to compromise servers and deploy cryptocurrency miners, with researchers reporting at least 21 affected systems, including 19 running the company's latest security update.
instructions: In a November 12 security advisory , N-able said it was implementing additional protections in response to the new disclosures, including restricting certain N-central features and integrations while it develops further fixes.
The protections have already been applied to hosted environments, but customers are also advised to continue upgrading their Agents and Probes under the previous Hotfix 2 guidance .

In its advisory, N-able said it had seen no signs of compromise using the new flaws, although security researchers have since reported successful exploitation of the vulnerability against production N-central servers.

Organizations running N-central should ensure that Legacy APIs are disabled and investigate suspicious requests to /dms/services/ServerUI , especially those referencing jline.internal.TerminalLineSettings.

items.title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
items.summary: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (also known as Nightmare Eclipse) has released a new Windows zero-day exploit that can let attackers gain SYSTEM privileges.
instructions: Naceri added that attacks exploiting CLFS vulnerabilities dropped sharply after the mitigation, but that Microsoft's mitigation itself introduced this new vulnerability.
Named SignDrop , it exploits mitigations Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to defend against authentication attacks targeting vulnerabilities in the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver.

Naceri noted that Microsoft implemented the mitigation properly but that "the logic allows abuse" and said the technique works against any antimalware engine's self-defense (tamper protection), because the file-creation request appears to come from the engine's own legitimate process.
"If everything is chained correctly, funnily, this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation of privileges.

instructions: Both research teams also recommend avoiding interactive ScreenConnect sessions with potentially infected endpoints and instead using separate security tools to investigate systems.

items.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
items.summary: A Lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform allowed researchers to take control of Kokoro, a text-to-speech model used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services.
instructions: Although its developer, Hexgrad, has not pushed an update since April 2025, the project continues to be popular, with nearly 13 million monthly downloads on Hugging Face.
Over the past weekend, the researchers registered the “hexgrad.com” domain listed on Kokoro’s public DONATE.md file and used it to perform a password reset on the publisher’s account.
The researcher underlines that an update would still carry all the hallmarks of a legitimate release, as tests from another account showed that Hugging Face would not flag anything as suspicious.
Hertz says even non-hijacked accounts could pose a risk, as anyone can curate an ostensibly legitimate image for a period of time, then push a malicious update at some point.

items.title: Your Endpoint Management Platform Could Be Your Biggest Security Risk
items.summary: Endpoint management platforms can become powerful attack tools when compromised, allowing hackers to deploy malware, execute commands, and disrupt thousands of devices. Action1 explains how customer-controlled cryptographic authorization can prevent attackers from abusing sensitive endpoint operations.
instructions: This security implication is: high-risk endpoint operations should have authorization that remains verifiable independently of the management platform delivering them!
Organizations should re-evaluate how these platforms are secured, how suspicious activity is monitored, and which protections remain effective if management infrastructure is compromised.
They allow administrators to deploy patches, install software, execute scripts, enforce configurations, and remotely manage thousands of devices from a centralized system.

Any attacker who gains control of that infrastructure will be able to use those existing capabilities to distribute malware, execute malicious commands, disable security controls, or disrupt operations across an entire organization.
